top_stories.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploited BeyondTrust Zero-Day to Take Over Remote Support Servers
top_stories.summary: A China-linked cyber espionage group tracked as Armory Castle exploited a critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-102764, CVSS 9.3) in BeyondTrust Remote Support to take over remote support servers. The flaw involves improper origin validation in an internal messaging component and was exploited in late August 2026.

top_stories.title: BeyondTrust patches zero-day exploited in attacks since August
top_stories.summary: BeyondTrust disclosed a critical zero-day vulnerability in its Remote Support product that has been actively exploited in attacks since August. The flaw required an emergency patch and affects BeyondTrust's privileged access management and remote support infrastructure.

top_stories.title: Hackers Use Compromised ConnectWise Credential to Sign In to 173 Microsoft 365 Tenants
top_stories.summary: Threat actors used a compromised ConnectWise Cloud Backup credential to gain unauthorized access to 173 Microsoft 365 tenants belonging to managed service providers and their customers. The attack highlights risks associated with shared service provider credentials and cross-tenant access in M365 environments.

top_stories.title: CISA Urges Immediate Ivanti Connect Secure Updates as Honeypots Log 105 Exploit Attempts
top_stories.summary: CISA is urging organizations to immediately update Ivanti Connect Secure appliances following active exploitation of CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass vulnerability with a CVSS score of 8.6. Honeypots have recorded 105 exploit attempts against the flaw, which affects the ICS remote access and VPN product.

top_stories.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support Zero-Day Continues Trend of Exploited Edge Bugs
top_stories.summary: A zero-day vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support has been actively exploited, joining a wave of edge device vulnerabilities affecting Ivanti, Cisco, and Palo Alto Networks in the same week. BeyondTrust is a privileged access management (PAM) vendor, making this directly relevant to IAM security practitioners managing remote and privileged access infrastructure.

news.title: Why Active Directory weaknesses stay open for years in teams with one or two admins
news.summary: An interview with intcube CTO David Fuhr details a 12-week security cohort where 27 municipalities collaboratively hardened Windows Server and Active Directory configurations. The program covered critical authentication and directory settings including SMB signing, LDAP signing, and Kerberos hardening, with lab testing used to validate changes before deployment.

news.title: UAT-11985 Uses Fake Event Invites to Target Taiwan Research Affiliates With Google AitM Phishing
news.summary: Researchers have disclosed details of an APT spear-phishing campaign (UAT-11985) targeting Taiwan research organization affiliates using fake event invites leading to an adversary-in-the-middle phishing framework. The campaign is designed to harvest Google account credentials and MFA codes, bypassing multi-factor authentication protections.

news.title: jumpserver v5.1.0
news.summary: JumpServer has released version 5.1.0 of its open-source Privileged Access Management platform. The platform provides DevOps and IT teams with secure access to SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, database, and RemoteApp endpoints via a web browser.

news.title: GhostAction Compromises About 1,900 GitHub Accounts, Targets Over 30,000 Repositories
news.summary: A credential-theft campaign called GhostAction compromised approximately 1,900 GitHub accounts and targeted over 30,000 repositories across 3,000 users and organizations. The attack, observed on October 8-9, 2026, attempted to extract 3,174 secrets from public repositories' CI pipelines, according to GitGuardian researchers.

news.title: Canonical releases Ubuntu 26.10 Stonking Stingray
news.summary: Canonical released Ubuntu 26.10 Stonking Stingray, an interim release that includes improvements to enterprise identity integration among other features. The release also adds post-quantum package signing, Rust coreutils, and privacy-focused speech-to-text capabilities.

news.title: Ivanti ICS Zero-Day Attacks Highlight Vendor Patching Hurdles
news.summary: A high-severity zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-104935) affecting Ivanti ICS combines authentication bypass and remote code execution, and was only partially discovered and patched in July. The incomplete patch left a window for threat actors to exploit the authentication bypass flaw in active attacks.

news.title: Anthropic 'SneakPeek' Flaw Is a Silent Zero-Click Threat
news.summary: A vulnerability dubbed "SneakPeek" in Anthropic's Claude Code Desktop application allows attackers to silently steal credentials including SSH private keys, AWS credentials, and OAuth tokens via the preview pane without requiring user interaction. The zero-click flaw enables credential theft from developers without any visible indicators of compromise.

news.title: Microsoft Disrupts 3 Phishing Kits Linked to Over 1 Billion Scam Messages
news.summary: Microsoft, alongside Health-ISAC, JC3, and private sector partners, disrupted three phishing kits—CoGUI, Haozi, and Iron Man System—linked to over 1 billion scam messages since January 2026. The operation involved companies including Resecurity, Cloudflare, Oracle, Proofpoint, and TRM Labs targeting credential-harvesting infrastructure.

news.title: Employees Built the Agents. Enterprises Just Bought the Supervisors.
news.summary: The article examines the emerging dual-lane enterprise AI agent landscape, distinguishing between IT-sanctioned agents managed through identity governance platforms like Okta and employee-built unsanctioned agents. The divide creates new challenges for identity governance and access management as enterprises attempt to monitor and control AI agents operating within their environments.

news.title: The hidden network: Inside the phishing infrastructure ecosystem powering global cybercrime
news.summary: Microsoft uncovered a Chinese-language cybercriminal ecosystem involving phishing kit operators (Storm-2990) and an illicit marketplace (Storm-3119) selling tools and infrastructure for large-scale phishing attacks. The operation targets credential theft and identity compromise at scale, with Microsoft collaborating on the investigation and takedown efforts.

news.title: Semperis 2026 Ransomware Report Reveals Increases in AI-Driven Attacks and a Rise in Physical Threats Against Executives and Their Families
news.summary: Semperis released its 2026 Ransomware Report highlighting increases in AI-driven attacks, repeat ransomware incidents, and attacks specifically targeting identity systems. The report also documents a rise in physical threats against executives and their families, with findings indicating that recovery readiness has not kept pace with the evolving threat landscape.

news.title: Workday Signs C1 Ai Deal to Govern People and Agents - El-Balad.com
news.summary: Workday signed a definitive agreement to acquire C1 AI on October 13, 2026, targeting governance of access for both human users and AI agents. The deal extends Workday's capabilities into identity governance territory, addressing the growing need to manage AI agent access alongside traditional workforce access.

news.title: Zero-Days Lurk in Microsoft's Overgrown October Patch Tuesday
news.summary: Microsoft's October Patch Tuesday, described as the largest security update ever, contains multiple zero-day vulnerabilities including defense bypasses and unauthenticated remote code execution flaws. The update is relevant to IAM professionals due to the presence of authentication-related bypass vulnerabilities in Microsoft's ecosystem.

news.title: No Identity, No Recovery: Cyber Resilience Starts With IAM
news.summary: The article argues that identity and access management is a foundational component of cyber resilience strategies. It focuses on the challenges posed by enterprise app proliferation and reliance on cloud identity providers.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record patch batch fixing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. The update is notable for its scale, with Microsoft attributing accelerated vulnerability discovery to AI assistance.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian drivers licenses, apparently sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company. The FBI's New Orleans field office has opened an official investigation into the breach.
